answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The marble multiplier is published, charged in beacon, and glacier lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1781 identities would post 2245 proofs and burn roughly 34 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
